audit.whatIsWrong: Two errors run through the whole entry. (a) Smoke Screen is described as a blind that 'negates your autos and Alpha Strike on-hit damage' in focus.text, loading, breakdown.cooldowns, dontsFull[0], report[5], whys[2], spikes[0], spikes[1], early and mid. Riot's text is a cloud that reduces sight range and slows on impact — it takes your vision, not your attacks. (b) Graves's Q is named 'Buckshot' in whys[1], spikes[0], spikes[2] and early; his Q is End of the Line. spikes[2] compounds it by calling the dash 'End of the Line dash' — the dash is Quickdraw (E). Armour stacking is also attributed to his passive; True Grit is on Quickdraw.
audit.why: The difference is the entire fight plan. If the smoke blinded you, the answer would be to wait it out with your damage off; because it only cuts sight range, your on-hit DPS is fully intact and the real cost is losing the target — so you step out of the cloud and keep hitting, rather than disengaging. Highlander's slow immunity does answer the impact slow, which the entry already had right.
audit.corrected: Smoke Screen restated as a sight-range cut everywhere it appears; End of the Line and Quickdraw named correctly; armour stacking moved to Quickdraw; Highlander's slow immunity stated as the answer to the smoke slow.

notes: Two systematic errors, both fixed everywhere they appear. 'Buckshot' is not Graves's Q — it is End of the Line — and spikes[2] called the dash 'End of the Line dash' when the dash is Quickdraw. More importantly, Smoke Screen was treated as an attack blind throughout; Riot's text gives it a sight-range reduction and an impact slow. That changed the advice from 'disengage until it fades' to 'keep hitting, just step out of the cloud so you can see him'. The Graves-side mirror made the same correction, so the two directions now agree.
